issues.description: Duplicated mode-to-bytes dispatch ladders in sign_message and verify_signature
issues.detail: chia/wallet/util/signing.py contains two parallel if/elif chains mapping SigningMode to the bytes that get signed/verified — once in sign_message() and once in verify_signature(). They have subtle asymmetries (sign_message falls through to CHIP_0002 for unknown modes; verify_signature raises). The central invariant of a signing library is that signed bytes equal verified bytes for every mode. Extract a single message_bytes_for(mode, message) -> bytes helper used by both sides so the invariant is enforced by construction.

issues.description: signing_mode_enum is non-exhaustive — silently falls through to CHIP_0002 for the fourth (is_hex, safe_mode) case
issues.detail: The free function signing_mode_enum() in wallet_request_types.py handles three of four (is_hex, safe_mode) combinations explicitly and returns CHIP_0002 by unguarded fallthrough for the fourth. Replace with a total function over the 2x2 truth table — a dict keyed by (is_hex, safe_mode) or an explicit final elif — so all four cases are visible and a future fifth case cannot silently land in CHIP_0002.

issues.description: signing_mode_enum exists three times in the same module — free function plus @property on two request classes
issues.detail: wallet_request_types.py defines a module-level signing_mode_enum(request) function and then a @property signing_mode_enum on both SignMessageByAddress and SignMessageByID that just forwards to the free function. Same name, three definitions, two scopes — easy to misread and invites future drift. Pick one form (the @property or a single helper keyed on the two booleans) and remove the others.

issues.description: convert_secret_key_to_synthetic is a stateless function masquerading as a Wallet method
issues.detail: Wallet.convert_secret_key_to_synthetic(self, secret_key) does not touch self — it is a one-line wrapper around calculate_synthetic_secret_key(secret_key, DEFAULT_HIDDEN_PUZZLE_HASH). Callers reach it via self.service.wallet_state_manager.main_wallet.convert_secret_key_to_synthetic(...), implying per-wallet behavior that does not exist. Move it to chia/wallet/util/signing.py (or alongside calculate_synthetic_secret_key) as a free function or @staticmethod.

issues.description: verify_signature is coupled to the RPC wire type VerifySignatureResponse
issues.detail: chia/wallet/util/signing.py imports VerifySignatureResponse from chia.wallet.wallet_request_types so it can construct one. The util — conceptually below the RPC layer — now depends on the RPC request-types module for its return shape, contradicting the stated goal of making signing reusable by other wallet areas. Return a small internal value (tuple[bool, str | None] or a local dataclass) and let the RPC layer translate it into the wire response.

issues.description: verify_signature docstring still references a 'request' parameter that no longer exists
issues.detail: The extracted verify_signature() carries ':param request:' / ':return:' from the prior RPC-method shape, even though it now takes five keyword arguments (signing_mode, public_key, message, signature, address). Update the docstring to describe each parameter and the address-binding semantics, or remove it.

issues.description: Variable name hex_message is misleading on non-hex code paths
issues.detail: In sign_message() the local hex_message holds a tree-hash digest in the CHIP_0002 default branch and a UTF-8 byte string in the BLS UTF-8 branch — only one of four cases is actually hex. Rename to message_to_sign to mirror message_to_verify in verify_signature() and remove a false invariant from the reader's eye.

The new RPC test calls rpc_client.verify_signature(...) but never asserts on the return value. VerifySignatureResponse carries an isValid bool and an optional error — an invalid signature would still return a response object without raising. Add `assert res.isValid is True` so the test actually pins the sign-then-verify postcondition.

issues.description: test_sign_message_by_nft_id does not assert signing_mode or pin the expected pubkey
issues.detail: The new test verifies AugSchemeMPL.verify(response.pubkey, expected_bytes, response.signature) — a tautology for any well-formed (pubkey, signature) pair the implementation returns. It does not assert that response.signing_mode reflects the requested (is_hex, safe_mode) combination, and it does not pin response.pubkey to the expected synthetic-of-inner-p2 key. Add per-case asserts on signing_mode (locking the truth table in signing_mode_enum) and derive the expected synthetic pubkey from the NFT's inner p2 puzzle hash and assert equality.

issues.description: SignMessageResponse dataclass adds no value over a 2-tuple
issues.detail: chia/wallet/util/signing.py introduces a new frozen kw_only dataclass with exactly two fields (pubkey, signature) that every call site immediately destructures back into the existing SignMessageByAddressResponse / SignMessageByIDResponse. The prior tuple[G1Element, G2Element] return was sufficient and matched the old per-wallet sign_message signatures. Drop the wrapper class and return the tuple, or have callers consume the response types directly.

issues.description: DID error message reworded without reason in a refactor PR
issues.detail: did_wallet.current_p2_puzzle_hash raises 'Invalid DID inner puzzle.' where the original code said 'Invalid inner DID puzzle.' Harmless but a gratuitous prose churn in a refactor — revert the wording or leave the original alone.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the direction is right: extracting sign_message/verify_signature into chia/wallet/util/signing.py and replacing per-wallet sign_message methods with current_p2_puzzle_hash helpers is the correct shape. But the extraction is mechanical rather than decomposed — the mode-to-bytes dispatch is duplicated as parallel if/elif ladders in sign_message and verify_signature, signing_mode_enum exists three times in the same module with a silent fallthrough over a 2x2 truth table, and verify_signature imports an RPC wire DTO (VerifySignatureResponse), coupling the new "library" back to wallet_request_types. Secondary residue includes a stateless convert_secret_key_to_synthetic placed on Wallet as an instance method, a stale ':param request:' docstring, a misleading hex_message variable name, and a gratuitously renamed DID error string. The new tests close a real gap but under-constrain behavior: one discards the verify result, the other asserts a signature against its own returned pubkey (tautological) and never pins signing_mode or the expected synthetic pubkey. Fix the dedup, make signing_mode_enum total, tighten the tests, and the patch lands.
